text:
maria: Heads-up: I ran a 2h gating experiment on the continuous batcher. Trying tokenflow gating to avoid large-KV thrash when long prompts spike.
sam: nice, what gating rule did you use? simple token ceiling or decode-rate aware?
maria: decode-rate aware. rule: if decode_rate < 10 tok/s and prompt_len > 4k -> prefer small micro-batch, else normal batching. config snippet:\n```
--gating.mode=decode_rate
--gating.decode_threshold=10
--gating.prompt_len_threshold=4096
--gating.token_budget_per_batch=2048
```
cheng: did you also adjust kv_prefetch budget? that seems related.
maria: yes. lowered kv_prefetch_budget for those micro-batches to 256 to reduce eviction churn. initial runs show 18% reduction in 95p latency regressions.
ryan: any effect on throughput / token/sec across the node?
maria: slight dip in aggregate tps (~3%) during the spike window, but tail latency improved a lot. overall cost per token down ~1.6% because we avoid repeated KV reloads.
eva: do you have perf traces? can you paste flame or p95 before/after?
maria: pasted a small trace snippet from the profiler below. p95 decode went from 420ms -> 310ms for long prompts. KV cache miss rate dropped from 22% -> 6% in the micro-batched cohort:\n```
TRACE: cohort=long_prompt_gated
decode_p95_before=420ms
decode_p95_after=310ms
kv_miss_before=0.22
kv_miss_after=0.06
```
perf-bot: [perf-run-id: pr-2026-03-14-09:12] 2 experiments completed, change: kv-prefetch budget reduced for gated cohort, decode-rate gating applied.
sam: sweet. any regressions for short prompts? sometimes gating steals capacity and hurts small ones.
maria: we saw a tiny 4% bump in short-prompt p50 during the tail of spikes, but p95 unchanged. hypothesis: admission policy moved a handful of short requests into smaller pools briefly.
cheng: can you share the admission policy rule? maybe add a weight so short prompts get N tokens guaranteed.
maria: current admission rule (simplified):
```
if cohort==long_gated -> prefer micro_pool
else -> normal_pool
```
will try adding `short_guarantee=128` next.
ryan: curious about kernel selection interplay. Did the micro-batches force different kernel paths? maybe quantized matmul channel got used.
maria: good call. for micro-batches we flip to the low-latency kernel which has better startup but lower throughput; that's why tps drops a bit.
eva: can we simulate with synthetic mixes? want to know sensitivity to spike frequency.
maria: yes, plan: run 6-hour sim with spike frequencies at 1/min, 1/5min, 1/20min. also ramp decode_rate thresholds 8/10/12.
sam: also log `kv_eviction_events` and `kernel_switch_count` per minute.
maria: will do. next steps: 1) run the sims 2) add `short_guarantee` to admission 3) evaluate cost delta. target: <2% cost increase, p95 long down >=15%. @cheng @ryan please weigh in if you want to change kernel thresholds.
cheng: ack. I'll run a quick microbenchmark to profile kernel handoff latency.
ryan: I'll check routing policy interactions (region/burst fallbacks) in case gating interacts badly with cross-region fallthrough.
eva: want results by EOD tomorrow for the oncall handover.
maria: noted. will post a short summary and attach perf-run IDs when done. :thumbsup:
